properties.name: Pioneer Seamount
properties.positionSource: Published summit 37°21.1'N 123°26.1'W, 820 m (GMRT 813 m)
properties.description: About 45 nmi WSW of Pillar Point. Top ~820 m. Pelagic structure on warm-water years.

properties.name: Guide Seamount
properties.positionSource: Published summit 37°00.6'N 123°21.0'W, 1,682 m (GMRT 1,671 m)
properties.description: About 50 nmi southwest of Pillar Point. Deep: primarily a navigation reference and longliner mark.

properties.name: Davidson Seamount
properties.positionSource: GMRT summit, 1,250 m (matches the published summit depth)
properties.description: About 80 mi WSW of Monterey. Top ~1,250 m, base 3,650 m. Within Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary; deep-sea coral / sponge habitat protected.

properties.name: Sur Ridge
properties.positionSource: GMRT ridge crest ~790 m; MBNMS: ridge 28 mi offshore, 817-1,569 m
properties.description: About 25-30 mi off Big Sur. Deep cold-water coral and sponge habitat. Inside Monterey Bay NMS.

properties.name: Monterey Canyon
properties.description: Largest submarine canyon on the US west coast. Drops from 100 m to 4,000+ m within a few miles of Moss Landing.

properties.name: Soquel Canyon
properties.description: North arm of Monterey Bay. Historic albacore grounds.

properties.name: Ascension Canyon
properties.description: Off Año Nuevo. Productive deep edge in fall albacore season.

properties.name: Carmel Canyon
properties.description: Off Pt. Lobos. Productive deep edge for rockfish and lingcod.

properties.name: Carmel Pinnacles
properties.positionSource: CDFW Carmel Pinnacles SMR boundary
properties.description: Inside Carmel Bay. Famous shore- and boat-launch dive — within Carmel Pinnacles SMR; check the MPAs layer for take rules.

properties.name: Pt. Sur
properties.description: Big Sur coast. Upwelling boundary — SST breaks consistently form here.

properties.name: Pt. Conception
properties.description: The thermal hinge of the California coast. Cold/warm divider — relevant context for any session north or south of it.

properties.name: Cojo / Government Point
properties.positionSource: GNIS (Cojo Anchorage); CP7 anchorage in 5-10 fathoms
properties.description: Famous lee anchorage just inside Pt. Conception. The classic wait-out for southbound boats when the point is howling.

properties.name: Naples Reef
properties.positionSource: GNIS
properties.description: Kelp-fringed reef off the Goleta coast. Popular shore-launch dive and freedive spot. Inside Naples SMCA.

properties.name: Anacapa West End / Cat Rock
properties.positionSource: GNIS (Cat Rock)
properties.description: Iconic dive and fishing spot at Anacapa Island's west tip. Partly inside the Anacapa SMR — see the MPAs layer for boundaries.

properties.name: The Footprint
properties.positionSource: GMRT summit (~96 m) inside the Footprint SMR/FMR polygon; least depth from the CDFW CRFS map's '47 fathom spot'
properties.description: Deep bank about 4 nmi southwest of West Anacapa, on the south side of Anacapa Passage. Inside the Footprint State and Federal Marine Reserves: no take.

properties.name: Yellowbanks
properties.positionSource: GNIS (Yellowbanks Anchorage), nearest 10-30 m water
properties.description: Off the southeast end of Santa Cruz Island. Reliable yellowtail when warm water pushes through the channel.

properties.name: Gull Island
properties.positionSource: GNIS
properties.description: South side of Santa Cruz Island. Sheltered hook-and-line and dive ground.

properties.name: San Miguel — Wyckoff Ledge
properties.positionSource: CP7: 1.4 mi west of Crook Point, 0.5 mi offshore, covered 1.5 fathoms
properties.description: Ledge off the south side of San Miguel Island, west of Crook Point. Cold-water big-fish territory: white seabass, halibut, big calicos.

properties.name: Talcott Shoal
properties.positionSource: CP7: 1.5 mi north-northeast of Sandy Point, least depth 1.75 fathoms
properties.description: Broad reef off the northwest corner of Santa Rosa Island. Productive in spring and fall.

properties.name: Potato Bank
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart; GMRT shows an isolated rise topping out near 90 m
properties.description: Isolated bank about 12 nmi west of San Nicolas Island. Pelagic structure on warm-water years.

properties.name: Tanner Bank
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart (GMRT ~35-45 m); CP7 least survey depth 9 fathoms
properties.description: Bank about 12 mi long and 5 mi wide, about 110 mi west of San Diego; least depth 9 fathoms. Tuna, yellowtail, and white seabass when the temp break aligns.

properties.name: Cortes Bank — Bishop Rock
properties.positionSource: CP7: Bishop Rock 'in about 32°27'N 119°08'W'; GMRT shallowest cell
properties.description: About 100 nmi WSW of San Diego. Bishop Rock is awash: the farthest outlying danger on the coast. Famous big-wave break and pelagic fishing destination.

properties.name: San Juan Seamount
properties.positionSource: GMRT summit, 553 m
properties.description: Far offshore. Deep — primarily of interest to longliners and oceanographers.

properties.name: Rodriguez Seamount
properties.positionSource: GMRT summit, 632 m (BD chart agrees)
properties.description: Far offshore. Top ~800 m. Pelagic structure on years when warm water reaches that far north.

properties.name: Farnsworth Bank
properties.positionSource: GNIS; CP7: 9.2 mi SSE of West End, 1.6 mi offshore, least depth 9 fathoms
properties.description: Off the back (southwest) side of Catalina. Premier white seabass and dive site, famous for purple hydrocoral. Inside the Farnsworth SMCAs: check the MPAs layer for take rules.

properties.name: Ship Rock
properties.positionSource: GNIS
properties.description: North end of Catalina. Reliable yellowtail boil spot when there's any current.

properties.name: Bird Rock
properties.positionSource: GNIS
properties.description: North end Catalina. Adjacent to Ship Rock — both fish on the same conditions.

properties.name: Casino Point Underwater Park
properties.positionSource: GNIS
properties.description: World-famous shore dive at Avalon. Inside the Casino Point Marine Park — no take.

properties.name: Blue Cavern Point
properties.positionSource: GNIS
properties.description: North Catalina. Classic dive site with healthy kelp forest.

properties.name: Empire Landing
properties.positionSource: GNIS, nearest ~9 m water
properties.description: Catalina inshore — productive sand-bass and calico spot.

properties.name: East End Quarry (Pebbly Beach)
properties.positionSource: Pebbly Beach quarry (OpenStreetMap), nearest ~18 m water
properties.description: Off the Pebbly Beach quarry, east of Avalon. Reliable late-summer yellowtail mark.

properties.name: Pyramid Cove
properties.positionSource: GNIS, nearest ~11 m water
properties.description: South end of San Clemente Island. Anchorage and yellowtail spot. Note: Navy range — closures common, check NOTMARs.

properties.name: Wilson Cove
properties.positionSource: GNIS, nearest ~10 m water
properties.description: Northeast San Clemente Island. Sheltered anchorage.

properties.name: NW Harbor
properties.positionSource: GNIS (Northwest Harbor)
properties.description: Northwest end of San Clemente Island.

properties.name: China Point
properties.positionSource: GNIS; CP7: southwest extremity of San Clemente Island
properties.description: Southwest tip of San Clemente Island, on the west side of Pyramid Cove. Navy range: closures are common, check NOTMARs.

properties.name: Castle Rock
properties.positionSource: GNIS; CP7: 0.4 mi off the northwest point
properties.description: Off northwest San Clemente Island. Pinnacle structure for yellowtail.

properties.name: 9 Mile Bank
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart ('North 9 Mile Bank'); GMRT top ~130 m
properties.description: About 10 nmi west of Point Loma. Sand bass year-round; reliable yellowtail when warm water pushes in.

properties.name: 14 Mile Bank
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart; GMRT top ~100 m
properties.description: In the San Pedro Channel about 14 mi SSW of Newport Harbor, toward Catalina's east end. Reliable summer-fall yellowtail and tuna ground.

properties.name: The 43 Spot
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart; GMRT ~80-86 m, matching its 43-fathom name
properties.description: Named for its 43-fathom chart sounding, about 37 nmi west of Point Loma.

properties.name: Pt. Loma Kelp
properties.positionSource: Inside the Point Loma kelp bed (GMRT ~11 m)
properties.description: Inshore kelp forest off Pt. Loma. Classic yellowtail / calico spot. Partly inside the Cabrillo SMR — see MPAs.

properties.name: The 209
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart; GMRT high ~381 m = 209 fathoms
properties.description: Named for its 209-fathom chart sounding, about 25 nmi WSW of Oceanside.

properties.name: The 267
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart; GMRT ~540 m (267 fathoms = 488 m)
properties.description: Named for its 267-fathom chart sounding, about 22 nmi west of Oceanside.

properties.name: The 277
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart; GMRT high ~456-507 m, matching 277 fathoms
properties.description: Named for its 277-fathom chart sounding, between Catalina and Oceanside about 15 nmi southeast of Avalon.

properties.name: The 302
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart; GMRT ~557-675 m (302 fathoms = 552 m)
properties.description: Named for its 302-fathom chart sounding, about 22 nmi southwest of Point Loma.

properties.name: The 312
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart; GMRT high ~569 m = 312 fathoms
properties.description: Named for its 312-fathom chart sounding, about 24 nmi southwest of Oceanside.

properties.name: The 1010 Trench
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart; GMRT ~1,845 m = 1,010 fathoms
properties.description: Deep trench off northern Baja about 60 nmi south-southwest of Point Loma, named for its 1,010-fathom sounding. Summer bluefin when the temp break aligns over it.

properties.name: 60 Mile Bank
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart (GMRT ~90-140 m); CP7: 62 mi from Point Loma, least depth 53 fathoms
properties.description: About 62 nmi southwest of Point Loma; least depth 53 fathoms. Premier offshore ground for yellowfin, bluefin, and yellowtail.

properties.name: The Mushroom
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart only (GMRT ~320-460 m); not independently confirmed
properties.description: Deep high spot about 13 nmi west of 60 Mile Bank, as placed on the BD Outdoors chart. Verify locally.

properties.name: The Hidden Bank
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart label position only; GMRT shows no shallow top nearby
properties.description: Offshore northern Baja, as placed on the BD Outdoors chart. Position approximate; verify locally.

properties.name: Northeast Bank
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart only (GMRT top ~360 m); not independently confirmed
properties.description: Deep bank west of Cortes Bank, as placed on the BD Outdoors chart. Verify locally.

properties.name: Mackerel Bank
properties.positionSource: BD Outdoors SoCal chart only (GMRT top ~630 m); not independently confirmed
properties.description: Deep bank east of the north end of San Clemente Island, as placed on the BD Outdoors chart. Verify locally.

properties.name: Cabrillo SMR (Pt. Loma tip)
properties.positionSource: CDFW Cabrillo SMR boundary (public/data/mpa-boundaries.geojson)
properties.description: Southern tip of Point Loma. Inside the Cabrillo SMR: no take, see the MPAs layer.

properties.name: Las Islas Coronado
properties.description: Four-island cluster (N/M/S + Pukey Point) about 15 mi south of the US border. Inside Mexico's Islas del Pacífico Biosphere Reserve — see CONANP.

properties.name: Salsipuedes
properties.positionSource: Bahía Salsipuedes; same point as the Salsipuedes spot in src/lib/mapData.js
properties.description: Kelp coast and reefs at Bahía Salsipuedes, north of Ensenada. Bottom fishing and white seabass. Mexican waters.

properties.name: Todos Santos Islands
properties.positionSource: Islas de Todos Santos, 31°48'N 116°48'W
properties.description: Off Ensenada. Killers reef — famous big-wave break. Mexican waters.
